subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept this custom cooperative glob walker and yielded bootstrap-hook scheduling as the bounded fix once exact-head performance proof is supplied?
rationale: The implementation targets a real P1 hot path without expanding public APIs, but it replaces dependency behavior and changes scheduling on compatibility-sensitive prompt and session surfaces.

options.title: Prove Exact Head, Then Land
options.body: Require a current-main versus current-head large-workspace run with event-loop ticks, total latency, peak RSS, matched files, and preferably a live embedded-run or channel probe before merging.

options.title: Accept Existing Proof
options.body: Treat the older direct-loader terminal comparison and focused parity tests as sufficient, then merge after exact-head checks while explicitly accepting compatibility and session-timing risk.

options.title: Pause the Custom Walker
options.body: Keep the PR open or narrow it to async reads and diagnostics while maintainers investigate a lower-maintenance glob or runtime-isolation design.

recommendation.title: Prove Exact Head, Then Land
recommendation.body: Require a current-main versus current-head large-workspace run with event-loop ticks, total latency, peak RSS, matched files, and preferably a live embedded-run or channel probe before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest merged-history connection spans all three decision surfaces: workspace reads, bootstrap hooks, and internal dispatch.
